gaps.sentence: He ___ spend so much time on his phone; it is affecting his sleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't' advises against an action: shouldn't spend.

gaps.sentence: Employees ___ use company computers for personal downloads.
gaps.hint: a formal prohibition with may not
gaps.explanation: Formal rules use 'may not' (or 'must not') for prohibitions: may not.

gaps.sentence: Do I ___ to bring my own towel, or is one provided?
gaps.hint: a question about necessity with do
gaps.explanation: Questions about necessity use 'do ... have to': have to bring.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better book now — the prices rise every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice, often with urgency: had better book.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better not be late again; the boss is getting tired of it.
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'had better' places 'not' after 'better': had better not be.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: It is the only blue house on the street, so you ___ miss it.
gaps.explanation: 'You can't miss it' is an idiom meaning it is impossible not to find: can't.

gaps.sentence: I ___ help thinking he is hiding something.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't help' plus -ing means being unable to stop a feeling: can't help thinking.
